primary_focus: Reusable component design: a self-contained async ActionButton (action prop + useTransition), generic ToggleGroup<T>, reusable ConfirmDialog on native <dialog>; failure paths that preserve user context.

checkpoints.title: Three regions render with labeled badges
checkpoints.requirement: The app renders the task creation form, the filter bar, and the task list; each task row shows its title plus status and priority badges with human-readable labels.
checkpoints.met_when: All three regions are present and task rows use the provided STATUS_LABELS / PRIORITY_LABELS (or equivalent human-readable text) for badges.
anti_patterns: Raw enum values ('in-progress') shown to the user
Badges conveyed by color alone with no text

checkpoints.title: Status transitions and delete work end to end
checkpoints.requirement: Each task shows exactly the action buttons for its status (Start / Complete / Reopen, plus Delete), the corresponding data-model API is called, and the list reflects the result on success.
checkpoints.met_when: Button visibility follows the status rules; updateTaskStatus / deleteTask from data-model.ts are used unmodified; task state updates only from the API result.
anti_patterns: All buttons always visible regardless of status
Local state mutated without calling the API, or API result ignored

checkpoints.title: Task creation flow works
checkpoints.requirement: The form creates a task via createTask with the entered title (required) and selected priority; the new task appears in the list; the form resets on success; Enter in the title input submits.
checkpoints.met_when: All listed behaviors are implemented, including Enter-to-submit by any mechanism.
checkpoints.partial_when: Creation works but one secondary behavior (reset on success, or Enter-to-submit) is missing.

checkpoints.title: Filters combine; two distinct empty states
checkpoints.requirement: Status and priority filters default to All, apply simultaneously (AND), and the two empty-state messages are distinguished: no-match vs no-tasks-at-all.
checkpoints.met_when: Both filters work together and the exact two messages from requirements 18-19 appear under the right conditions.
checkpoints.partial_when: Filtering is correct but the two empty states are conflated into one message.

checkpoints.title: API failure leaves state unchanged and notifies
checkpoints.requirement: When any API call fails (10% chance), a brief error notification is shown, the task state is not changed, and the app remains fully usable.
checkpoints.met_when: Failures are caught for all four APIs; task state only ever updates from a resolved API result; a user-visible notification appears.
checkpoints.partial_when: Failures are handled for some actions but at least one path swallows the error or leaves inconsistent state.
anti_patterns: Unhandled promise rejection (no catch) on any action path
State updated before the API resolves with no recovery on failure

checkpoints.title: Independent concurrent pending states
checkpoints.requirement: While a call is in flight, only the triggering button shows its pending label and disabled appearance; other buttons on the same and other tasks stay interactive, and multiple actions can be in flight simultaneously, each with its own pending state.
checkpoints.met_when: Pending state is tracked per button instance (not globally); a rapid second activation of the same button is prevented while pending.
anti_patterns: A single global isLoading that disables the whole board
Pending state keyed per task (not per button), so Start and Delete on the same task lock each other

checkpoints.title: App decomposed beyond the three required reusables
checkpoints.requirement: The application is decomposed into single-responsibility components beyond the three mandated reusables: the task list, the individual task row, and the creation form each exist as their own components rather than being inlined in App.
checkpoints.met_when: App composes distinct list / row / form components (names may vary); no component mixes unrelated responsibilities; App is a thin composition root.
checkpoints.partial_when: Some extraction exists but one major region (list rows or the form) is still inlined in a large App component.
anti_patterns: A ~200-line monolithic App containing rows, form, and dialog logic inline

checkpoints.title: One pending-button component used everywhere
checkpoints.requirement: The pending-state button behavior is a single reusable component used for all async buttons: the four task actions, the Create button, and the dialog's confirm button.
checkpoints.met_when: One component implements label-swap + disabled-while-pending, and every async button in the app is an instance of it.
checkpoints.partial_when: The component exists and covers most buttons, but at least one async button reimplements pending logic bespoke.
anti_patterns: Pending logic duplicated per call site with inline useState
The dialog's Delete button bypassing the shared component

checkpoints.title: The button owns its pending state
checkpoints.requirement: The reusable button manages pending state internally; call sites never manage or pass pending state.
checkpoints.met_when: No pending/loading boolean prop exists on the button API, and no call site holds useState for pending.
anti_patterns: A pending: boolean prop forcing every call site to run its own useState + try/finally — the pending lifecycle leaks to consumers

checkpoints.title: Single generic ToggleGroup for both filters
checkpoints.requirement: Both filters use one reusable toggle-group component whose value/options/onChange are typed by a generic parameter, so each call site gets its own precise value type.
checkpoints.met_when: One component with a type parameter (e.g. <T extends string>) serves both filters; onChange at the status call site receives the status union, not string.
checkpoints.partial_when: One shared component, but typed with plain string — call sites lose type safety.
anti_patterns: Two separate filter components with duplicated toggle logic

checkpoints.title: Filtered list and empty-state derived, not stored
checkpoints.requirement: The visible task list and the empty-state message are derived during render from tasks + filters; they are never mirrored into state or synced via effects.
checkpoints.met_when: No useState holds the filtered list or the message; no effect recomputes them (AP-01/AP-03 absent).
anti_patterns: AP-01: filteredTasks state updated by an effect watching tasks/filters

checkpoints.title: ConfirmDialog is reusable and task-agnostic
checkpoints.requirement: The confirmation dialog is a reusable component with message, labels, and confirm/cancel behavior supplied via props — nothing task-deletion-specific inside it — and Escape or clicking outside closes it without confirming.
checkpoints.met_when: The dialog component contains no task/domain logic; Escape and outside-click both cancel.
checkpoints.partial_when: Reusable API but one dismissal path (Escape or outside-click) is missing.
anti_patterns: Deletion confirmation hardcoded inside the task row component

checkpoints.title: Enter submits through the same pending pathway
checkpoints.requirement: The creation form uses a real <form> whose submit button is the shared pending button, so keyboard (Enter) and mouse submission exercise identical pending and error handling.
checkpoints.met_when: Enter triggers native form submission routed through the same code path as clicking Create — pending label shows and failures notify on both paths.
anti_patterns: onKeyDown Enter handler on the input reimplementing submission
type="button" + form onSubmit calling the API directly, so Enter submissions show no pending state and bypass error handling

checkpoints.title: Async status is communicated to assistive technology
checkpoints.requirement: Pending and error states are exposed to AT: pending buttons carry aria-busy (with the changed label), and error notifications use role="alert" or an assertive live region.
checkpoints.met_when: Both signals present: aria-busy={pending} on the shared button, and role="alert" (or aria-live="assertive") on error notifications.
checkpoints.partial_when: Exactly one of the two signals is present (e.g. aria-busy but errors only aria-live="polite", or vice versa).
anti_patterns: Pending conveyed only visually
Errors in a polite/status region that screen readers may never announce promptly

checkpoints.title: Initial fetch is a single clean mount effect
checkpoints.requirement: Initial tasks load via one mount-time mechanism with a loading indication and protection against state updates after unmount/re-run (or an equivalent Suspense-based approach).
checkpoints.met_when: Exactly one fetch path: a mount effect with an ignore/cancellation guard in cleanup (or use()/Suspense); loading state shown; no refetch loops.
checkpoints.partial_when: Single clean effect but no cancellation guard.
anti_patterns: AP-07: fetch effect with no dependency array
Fetch triggered from render or from multiple competing effects

checkpoints.title: Dialog dismissal wiring is stable and clean
checkpoints.requirement: Any manually implemented dialog dismissal listeners (document keydown for Escape, backdrop handlers) are attached once with stable dependencies and cleaned up; no ref-sync effects smuggle callbacks. Trivially met when the native <dialog> handles dismissal.
checkpoints.met_when: Native <dialog> dismissal, or manual listeners in a single effect with correct deps and cleanup, without useEffect-based ref syncing of handlers.
anti_patterns: Listener re-attached every render due to an unstable handler dependency
useEffect(() => { onCloseRef.current = onClose }) ref-sync effects (the manual useEffectEvent workaround)

checkpoints.title: Precise types throughout
checkpoints.requirement: The data-model types are used as-is, all component props have named types, and there is no any (including as any / suppressions) or untyped escape hatch.
checkpoints.met_when: Task/TaskStatus/TaskPriority imported and used; props typed via named interface/type; zero any; unions preserved (no widening to string).
anti_patterns: Loosely typed callbacks like () => Promise<unknown> where void is meant
Redeclaring local copies of the provided types

checkpoints.title: No reflexive memoization
checkpoints.requirement: Memoization appears only where a consumer justifies it; cheap values and handlers are not blanket-wrapped in useMemo/useCallback (AP-09), and no memoized child receives freshly created object/array props that defeat it.
checkpoints.met_when: Every useMemo/useCallback/React.memo present has an identifiable justification, or none are used at all — both are acceptable at this app's scale.
anti_patterns: AP-09: most values/handlers wrapped with no memoized consumers

checkpoints.title: Pending state is declarative: useTransition or form actions
checkpoints.requirement: The reusable button derives its pending state from React's async primitives — useTransition/startTransition wrapping the action, or an equivalent form-action integration (form action + useActionState/useFormStatus) — rather than manually flipping a useState boolean around the await.
checkpoints.met_when: isPending comes from useTransition (or useFormStatus/useActionState in a form-action design) inside the reusable button, for all async buttons.
checkpoints.partial_when: A transition/form-action drives some buttons (e.g. the form submit via useFormStatus) while others still use manual useState pending.
anti_patterns: const [pending, setPending] = useState(false) with setPending(true) before the call and finally setPending(false) — the imperative pattern React 19's transitions replace

checkpoints.title: Async contract expressed as an action prop
checkpoints.requirement: The reusable button's API names its async callback action (typed () => void | Promise<void> or () => Promise<void>), following the React 19 convention that signals the component owns the async lifecycle — not onClick.
checkpoints.met_when: The prop is named action (or a *Action name) with an async-aware type, and consumers pass the async operation directly.
anti_patterns: onClick: () => Promise<unknown> — reuses the sync-click name for an async contract, hiding that the component manages pending state

checkpoints.title: Native <dialog> with showModal()
checkpoints.requirement: The confirmation dialog is the native <dialog> element opened with showModal(), giving top-layer rendering, focus containment, Escape handling, and backdrop for free.
checkpoints.met_when: A <dialog> element and showModal()/close() calls exist; Escape/backdrop behavior builds on the native element (light-dismiss or a cancel/click handler on the dialog).
checkpoints.partial_when: <dialog> is used but opened via the open attribute instead of showModal(), losing modality and focus containment.
anti_patterns: A div overlay with role="dialog" aria-modal="true" plus hand-rolled Escape/backdrop effects — reimplements what the platform provides

checkpoints.title: Focus moves into the dialog and returns on close
checkpoints.requirement: Opening the dialog moves keyboard focus inside it and keeps it contained; closing returns focus to the element that opened it (native <dialog> modality, or equivalent manual management).
checkpoints.met_when: Focus lands in the dialog on open, cannot Tab out while open, and returns to the triggering Delete button on close — via showModal() semantics or explicit trap + restore code.
checkpoints.partial_when: Focus moves into the dialog (e.g. autoFocus) but is not contained or not restored on close.
anti_patterns: Focus left on the (possibly removed) trigger while the dialog is open, or dropped to <body> after closing

checkpoints.title: Failure paths preserve user context
checkpoints.requirement: When an API call fails, the user's context is preserved for retry: a failed delete leaves the confirmation dialog open with the error shown, and a failed creation keeps the form's entered values.
checkpoints.met_when: Both: the dialog closes only on successful deletion, and the form resets only on successful creation.
checkpoints.partial_when: Exactly one of the two failure paths preserves context.
anti_patterns: Dialog closed unconditionally in a finally block, discarding the user's intent on failure
Form cleared before the createTask promise resolves

checkpoints.title: Button composes native button props
checkpoints.requirement: The reusable button extends the native button's prop surface (e.g. Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<"button">, "onClick">) so consumers can pass type, disabled, aria-*, etc. with full type safety, instead of an ad-hoc closed prop list.
checkpoints.met_when: The props type derives from React's native button props with the superseded members omitted, and spreads the rest onto <button>.
anti_patterns: A closed hand-picked prop list that silently drops type="submit" or aria attributes
Spreading an untyped rest ({ ...props }: any) instead of deriving the type

checkpoints.title: Form inputs have real label associations
checkpoints.requirement: The title input and priority select are labeled via <label htmlFor> or wrapping <label> (visually hidden is fine given the placeholder-style layout), not bare aria-label strings.
checkpoints.met_when: Both form controls have an associated <label> element.
checkpoints.partial_when: One control has a real label, the other only aria-label.
anti_patterns: aria-label as the only labeling on native form controls that could carry real labels
